sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully encodes the in-area applicability, frame-owned paths, paired reciprocal attachments, conditional alternatives, exact two-side requirement, bracket stiffening, and millimetre thickness comparison without imposing support existence.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The COMPLETE dependency contract is not fully encoded: nltl:frameAttachment, nltl:hasAttachedSupportingStructure, and nltl:supportingStructure are omitted. Add the canonical nltl:frameAttachment path in its supplied frame-owned role, place nltl:hasAttachedSupportingStructure only on the frame-attachment owner, and constrain linked support values as nltl:supportingStructure. Use the attachment-to-support relationship to pair each applicable attachment with the specific supporting structure in the effective-attachment and longitudinal-bracket checks; the transverse termination alternative must likewise apply to the relevant attachment rather than allowing any unrelated attachment with a bracket or similar-construction flag to satisfy it. Preserve the universal semantics without adding unconditional support existence.

Repair the through-structure condition so nltl:webPlateConnectionSideCount is exactly 2, using equal sh:minInclusive and sh:maxInclusive bounds of 2; the current lower bound permits invalid counts above two even though the requirement is specifically that both web-plate sides are connected. Also scope the transverse termination bracket-or-similar alternative to the attachment paired with the relevant supporting structure; the current sh:node constraint applies it conjunctively to every frame attachment, including unrelated attachments. Preserve the existing frame-to-attachment, attachment-to-support, and reciprocal support-to-attachment pairing required by the prior feedback.

Scope the installed-bracket constraints to frames within the ice-strengthened area. The globally targeted gen:ConnectionBracketShape currently requires thickness and both stiffening flags for every bracket, including brackets belonging to out-of-scope frames, while the frame-thickness presence and thickness-comparison queries likewise omit nltl:withinIceStrengthenedArea true. Remove the unconditional bracket target or its mandatory constraints and enforce bracket thickness, frame web thickness, the bracket-thickness >= frame-web-thickness comparison, and the required true stiffening values only for brackets reached through attachments of in-area frames. Preserve the prior attachment-to-specific-support and reciprocal pairing, the bracket-or-similar alternative on that paired attachment, and the exact two-side bounds.

Candidate faithfully encodes the in-area applicability, frame-owned paths, paired reciprocal attachments, conditional alternatives, exact two-side requirement, bracket stiffening, and millimetre thickness comparison without imposing support existence.
